text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is a city in y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
DifferentStates(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states.
UniqueState(x) ::: x is in only one state.
Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ State(Montana) ∧ InCity(Billings, Montana) ::: Billings is a city in Montana.
InCity(Butte, Montana) ∧ InCity(Helena, Montana) ∧ InCity(Missoula, Montana) ::: The cities of Butte, Helena, and Missoula are in Montana.
InCity(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
InCity(StPierre, notMontana) ::: The city of St Pierre is not in Montana.
¬InCity(Butte, StPierre) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InCity(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y (City(x) ∧ City(y) ∧ x ≠ y → (InSameState(x, y) ∨ DifferentStates(x, y))) ::: A city can only be in one state in U.S. except for specific cities.
Conclusion:
InSameState(Butte, StPierre) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in the same state.
